subject: [RFC PATCH 0/4] mm/zswap: make shrinker writeback work with iocost

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Reviewer Christoph Hellwig questioned whether REQ_BACKGROUND truly allows for throttling of I/O operations, suggesting that it implies the operation can be throttled and thus the caller should not expect foreground paging.
sentiment_signals: requested clarification on I/O throttling implications
reviews.raw_body:
Is that true?  REQ_BACKGROUND very much implies the I/O can the throttled
and thus better not be foreground paging, and thus the caller should be
able to tolerate a failure.

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the performance of zswap shrinker on systems running iocost by addressing two issues: (1) zswap writeback is issued as root and charged to the cgroup afterwards, causing stalls in application allocations; and (2) throttled writes sleep in their submitter, often an application thread. The patches modify zswap to mark writebacks as REQ_BACKGROUND instead of REQ_SWAP, allowing them to be throttled by iocost controllers. Additionally, patch 4 moves reclaim-driven writeback to a per-lruvec kworker, reducing the impact on application threads. The series includes benchmarks showing significant performance improvements for various workloads.

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the shrinker writeback should be done in a way that allows for proper accounting of IO costs, and suggested using iocost's throttling mechanism to control the rate at which writebacks occur.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti questioned the necessity of marking zswap writebacks as REQ_BACKGROUND, citing that they are already best effort and failure does not impact the compressed entry's presence.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Christoph,

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 11:44 AM Christoph Hellwig <hch@infradead.org> wrote:

---

Yes, I agree, zswap writebacks are only best effort and in case of
failure, the compressed entry still lives. I don't see how
REQ_BACKGROUND could be an issue there?

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary: Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed concern about the scalability of adding multiple kworker threads for zswap writeback, suggesting alternatives such as per-cpu or global threading and inquiring about work accounting from a cgroup perspective.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah that tracks with an older experiment of mine, where I add some
manual throttling to zswap shrinker to reduce latency :) So I think
this problem is real - thanks for root-causing this, Alex!

I'm a bit nervous about adding multiple kworker threads though, hmmm.
Per-lruvec sounds like a lot of threads... Do we have to scale this by
lruvec? Why not per-cpu, or just a global thread? Is there any data to
support this autoscaling?

And do we have any concerns with work (CPU) accounting, from a cgroup
perspective...?

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed skepticism about the complexity of the proposed solution, implying that it may be overly complicated and requested a clearer explanation.

Reviewer Nhat Pham questioned whether moving writeback to a per-lruvec kworker would prevent the writeback submission from scaling with the number of tasks entering reclaim, and asked if writeback submission for proactive reclaimer and kswapd should be deferred.

The reviewer noted that the proposed change to zswap writeback will break the shrinker control loop, as the accumulation of writebacks in the shrinker API will grow over time, and requested a check be made to do_shrink_slab() in mm/shrinker.c.

Reviewer Nhat Pham noted that the patch changes the workqueue from single-threaded to multi-threaded and suggested adding a mention of this change in the changelog.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 9:23 AM Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr> wrote:

I understand the problem this patch is trying to solve, but this
solution seems more involved than the changelog suggests :)

---

Ahhh, so it's one work-item (added to the shared shrink_wq)
per-lruvec, not one kworker or thread per-lruvec.

Hmm, supposed multiple tasks in a cgroup enter direct reclaim. In the
past, the amount of writeback submission will scale with the number of
tasks entering reclaim. But now, it's just a single work item
per-lruvec - IIUC, the submission of his work item is idempotent, so
it wouldn't scale like that anymore, right? I haven't wrapped quite
wrapped my head around this, but this sounds like a non-trivial
effect...

Also, do we need to defer writeback submission for proactive
reclaimer? Or kswapd? Only direct reclaimers have concerns with the
latency blowup from the throttling right?

There are a couple more behavioural changes, without proper
justifcation or mentioning in the changelog. More details inlined
below:

---

This will have effect on the shrinker control loop too, right?
Shrinker API accumulates the number of writebacks overtime based on
shrinker_count()'s output, and we serve that number of writebacks
throgh shrinker_scan(). With this basically that accumulation just
grows over time, correct? Check do_shrink_slab() in mm/shrinker.c...

Feels like this completely breaks that control loop.

---

This turns a single-threaded workqueue into multi-threaded workqueue, IIUC.

Worth at least an callout in the changelog?
